answer: Graders run a mirror test each epoch: answers are embedded and compared, and any cluster of near-duplicate texts from different identities shares a single reward instead of each copy earning one. A sockpuppet farm must then pay for fifty bonds plus fifty separate compute budgets to write truly distinct text, so the payoff per fake identity falls from its zenith to near zero. It works like a jetty that charges one mooring fee per hull: lashing extra boats to it costs more than the dock pays out.
